A federal moratorium cannot pass a Trump veto and the Texas governor does not take office until January, so I judge the demand hit to chips over a 12-month horizon smaller than the one-day repricing, while accepting that sentiment can stay depressed for weeks. Fundamentals confirmed this week: ANET Q3 revenue +58.5% y/y to $3.66B vs $3.3B guide, FY26 guide raised a fourth time to $13.3B and 2027 guided to 38-40% growth vs ~30% consensus; Lam authorized a $25B buyback. Friday 11-06 saw a partial bounce (SMH +3.6%, TSM +6.3%, ANET +7.3%, MU +5.1%, NVDA +2.8%) but the Nasdaq still logged a fourth straight weekly loss (-3.4%). Macro is hostile to long-duration growth: October payrolls +165k vs ~60k expected, unemployment 4.1%, 10y 4.87%, 30y ~5.25%, December hike odds ~77%. NVDA reports 2026-11-17, a binary catalyst inside this holding period. BTC fell ~6% to ~$75k on ~$1B of leveraged liquidations and spot-ETF outflows, tracking the Nasdaq. Balancing these: this book has now been stopped out five times re-entering the same names after washouts, which says I have repeatedly been early in a downtrend. So I rebuild at 42% gross rather than 63%, drop AMD (chased an 11% Friday bounce), cut MU to 5% (highest beta, -27% realized, Taiwan fab labor dispute), overweight ANET (the only name with a fresh fundamental confirmation), and set equity stops at 12-15% so each sits below the 11-05 panic low with cushion: a full stop-out of every equity leg now costs ~4.5% of NAV instead of ~10%. Cash at 58% earns 4% while the policy picture and NVDA's print resolve. This is a considered, researched replacement of the provisional HOLD.
